name: A10 Mini V4
identify: helperFunctions.sh: /proc/cpuinfo part 0xd04 (RK3326) + /etc/os-release OS_NAME=DARKMOSS, SPRUCE_PLATFORM=A10MiniV4 (A10Mini whose device-tree model also contains "V4")

pad.from: measured: the lab capturesA10MiniV4-20261104.txt (node name only; individual button presses not captured)
pad.note: odroidgo3-joypad driver; carries the face buttons, d-pad, L1/R1/L2/R2, SELECT/START/L3/R3/MENU as BTN_TRIGGER_HAPPY1-5

power.from: measured: the lab capturesA10MiniV4-20261104.txt (node name only; individual button presses not captured)

vol.from: derived: A10MiniV4 discovery capture (the lab capturesA10MiniV4-20261104.txt) shows a 4th node "odroidgo3-keys" (event3, kbd) beside the pwrkey and the pad; dArkMossCommon.sh's resolve_key_event_node() re-points EVENT_PATH_VOLUME at whichever node's capability bits report both KEY_VOLUMEUP/DOWN, which the cfg's static event0 guess does not account for. Not confirmed this is that node: a hardware run should press VOL+/VOL- and see which /dev/input/eventN fires.
vol.note: cfg literally sets EVENT_PATH_VOLUME=EVENT_PATH_POWER (event0); this may be overridden at boot

absent.L3: no F3 on the A10 Mini V4 (tester 2026-11-12; button-reader-A10MiniV4-1.txt: no input on the step); A10MiniV4.cfg still lists B_L3/B_R3 1 706/1 707, the A10 Mini's F3/F4
absent.R3: no F4 on the A10 Mini V4 (tester 2026-11-12; button-reader-A10MiniV4-1.txt: no input on the step); A10MiniV4.cfg still lists B_L3/B_R3 1 706/1 707, the A10 Mini's F3/F4
absent.LEFT_STICK: no analog stick (DEVICE_NUM_ANALOG_STICKS=0); the d-pad can be switched to drive the same ABS_X/ABS_Y the STICK_* cfg vars name (odroidgo3-joypad's dpad_analog attribute), but that is a software mode swap of the d-pad, not a second control

notes: A10Mini.cfg's own header: "Pad, panel and SoC values are from the kernel dts ... and dArkOS's RG351MP configs; none of it has been read off a running unit yet." Every button code here is therefore cfg-level, not measured, even though A10MiniV4 has been booted in the lab (its discovery capture confirms the pad node name and that the unit boots, not individual button presses).

No analog stick (DEVICE_NUM_ANALOG_STICKS=0), but the odroidgo3-joypad driver can report the d-pad as the left stick instead (A10Mini.sh's DPAD_ANALOG sysfs toggle, swapped by MENU+SELECT in game): a software mode, not a second physical control.

L3/R3 (1 706/1 707) are two of the five BTN_TRIGGER_HAPPY1-5 buttons the odroidgo3-joypad driver exposes (select, start, L3, R3, the F/MENU key); the cfg comment describes them as real physical buttons on this stickless board, not stick clicks.
